Maine Gun Safety Coalition Testimony in SUPPORT of LD 1487: An Act to Support Community Violence Prevention and Intervention Programs
Senator Ingwerson, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Nacole Palmer, and I serve as executive director of the Maine Gun Safety Coalition.
I used to believe that violence--and specifically gun violence--was something that I would surely never have to encounter in my life. Perhaps you remember having felt that way at some point in your life, too. I thought gun violence sounded terrible, don't get me wrong. But it was something that other people in other places would have to deal with...surely not me. That was before a friend of mine in 7th grade was beaten with a gun and ultimately killed. Before the mass shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary took 20 children half an hour from my then-home in Connecticut. Before a gun took the life of one of my family members. Before the Lewiston mass shootings took 18 beloved Mainers, including the son of my friend Arthur Barnard, half an hour from where I live now. Before the weekly and sometimes daily news of shootings on Maine streets in Lewiston, or Sabattus, or Portland.
The sad truth that I have learned, and what I imagine we have all learned to some extent, is that no place and no person is immune from gun violence--no matter how much we may want to convince ourselves otherwise. I also believe that passivity in the face of the sheer number of gun tragedies that take our fellow citizens amounts to complicity. This problem will not solve itself...clearly. It will, in fact, take all of us.
The creation of the Maine Office of Violence Prevention in the wake of the Lewiston mass shootings of 2023 was a welcome development, and I was proud that this body passed that bill, initiated by Governor Mills, into law last year. In doing so, Maine joined about a dozen other states that have similar offices. The office just got a director this calendar year and is still in the process of hiring staff, as I understand it. I am hopeful that under the leadership of Director Bourque, the office will do great work to prevent violence in our state.

The work of preventing violence, including gun violence, has many facets. In addition to strong laws, prevening violence takes time, people, and accurate data. And all of those things take resources.
I don't need to tell you that funding for pretty much anything in our government is uncertain right now. We live in an incredibly uncertain time. This law would allow for the office to seek the funding it needs to do its excellent and much needed work of saving Maine lives.
I hope that it will gain the unanimous support of this committee, which I believe it deserves. And I thank you for your consideration. Please vote Ought to Pass for LD 1487.

THE MAINE SENATE

Testimony of Senator Rachel Talbot Ross introducing
LD 1487, "An Act to Support Community Violence Prevention and Intervention
Programs"
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
April 14, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee, I am Senator Rachel Talbot Ross. I represent Senate District 28, which includes part of my
hometown of Portland and Peaks Island.
Thank you for the opportunity to present LD l487, "An Act to Support Community Violence Prevention
and Intervention Programs."
This bill is a simple but essential step forward for the Office of Violence Prevention within the Maine
Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Specifically, LD 1487 authorizes the Office to seek and accept funding from any source -- federal, state, county, municipal, or private ----- to support its work.
This authority is common sense and consistent with how we fund many of Maine's public health efforts. By enabling programs to access grants and external funding opportunities, we not only leverage federal
and private dollars to support our cormnunities but also help reduce the tax burden on Maine residents.
This bill also builds on this Committee's work during the Second Session of the 131st Legislature.
LD 2237, "An Act to Strengthen Public Safety, Health and Well-being by Expanding Services and
Coordinating Violence Prevention Resources," was a comprehensive response to Maine's growing need
for system-level violence prevention efforts. That bill proposed various reforms -- including expanding
mobile crisis response services, establishing new crisis receiving centers, and creating the Office of
Violence Prevention within the Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention.
While much of LD 2237's language -- including the section establishing the Office -- was ultimately
carried into the state budget, this Committee made clear in its deliberations that this Office would be an
essential tool for coordinating violence prevention efforts statewide.
However, in its final version, LD 2237 did not include authority for the Office to receive or apply for outside funding. LD 1487 would add that necessary authority, ensuring that the Office of Violence
Prevention can pursue federal, private, and philanthropic funds to support its mission.
This is a natural next step in the development of the Office and an opportunity to bring in additional resources to support Maine's communities.

The Office of Violence Prevention is still relatively new, established during the 131st Legislature. It was
created to coordinate and promote effective violence prevention efforts statewide -- including public education campaigns, research, and community-based intervention strategies -- with a focus on reducing
gun violence and related trauma.
Many of us were involved in creating this Office, and while its foundational work is now underway, it
will need sustainable funding streams to achieve its full potential. Allowing the Office to pursue outside funding will ensure it has access to resources necessary to support Maine communities ----- especially those most impacted by violence.
importantly, this authority also aligns with the Office's existing work. The Office is charged with
identifying and promoting evidence-based strategies for violence prevention. Many of those strategies ---- from community violence intervention programs to trauma-informed outreach -- are supported by
national grant programs and philanthropic partners eager to invest in local solutions.
LD 1487 ensures that Maine will not leave those dollars on the table.
This straightforward and responsible bill strengthens an Office in which this Committee has already invested. It gives the Office of Violence Prevention the tools it needs to support local communities, expand its programming, and sustain its work over the long term.
I respectfully urge the Committee to support LD 1487.
Thank you for your time and for your commitment to public health and safety in Maine. I am happy to answer any questions you may have.
Sincerely,
Rachel Talbot Ross State Senator, District 28 Representing part ofPortland and Peaks Island
